test_environment.testing_method: Automated scanning with controlled test requests

test_cases.expected_result: Scanner identifies missing security headers such as Content-Security-Policy and X-Frame-Options.
limitations: HSTS should only be evaluated on HTTPS responses.
X-Frame-Options may be replaced by an appropriate CSP frame-ancestors directive.

test_cases.vulnerability_tested: Missing or incorrectly configured security headers
test_cases.expected_result: Scanner does not report missing headers that are correctly configured.
limitations: Header presence alone does not prove that the security policy is sufficiently restrictive.

test_cases.vulnerability_tested: Wildcard CORS origin combined with credentials
test_cases.expected_result: Scanner identifies an unsafe wildcard origin and credential configuration.
limitations: CORS behavior depends on the actual response headers and browser enforcement.
A wildcard origin with credentials may be rejected by browsers, so the finding should be interpreted as a configuration issue rather than proof of exploitable access.

test_cases.vulnerability_tested: Overly permissive or unrestricted CORS configuration
test_cases.expected_result: Scanner does not report the restricted and correctly configured CORS policy as an unsafe wildcard configuration.
limitations: The scanner's tested Origin may not cover every possible origin-handling behavior.

test_cases.vulnerability_tested: Missing HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite cookie attributes
test_cases.expected_result: Scanner identifies missing cookie security attributes in Set-Cookie responses.
limitations: Cookie checks require an endpoint that actually returns Set-Cookie headers.
Secure cookie behavior should be evaluated over HTTPS.
Cookie requirements can differ depending on the application's authentication design.

test_cases.expected_result: Scanner does not report missing attributes when the relevant cookies have correctly configured flags.
limitations: Only cookies returned by the endpoints visited during scanning are evaluated.

test_cases.vulnerability_tested: Absence of observable login rate limiting
test_cases.expected_result: Scanner reports that no rate-limiting behavior was observed after a bounded number of invalid login attempts.
limitations: A small number of requests cannot prove that rate limiting is completely absent.
Rate limiting may be implemented at a proxy, gateway, or infrastructure layer.
Only the configured login endpoint is tested.

test_cases.expected_result: Scanner observes rate-limiting evidence such as HTTP 429, an appropriate Retry-After header, or a relevant rate-limit signal.
limitations: A rate-limit response is evidence of rate limiting but does not establish that the implementation is effective against every brute-force strategy.
HTTP 423 alone may indicate a locked account rather than rate limiting.

overall_limitations: Evaluation is limited to the endpoints and responses accessible to the scanner.
Detection results depend on the accuracy of the demo application's vulnerable and hardened configurations.
Automated checks cannot establish the absence of every possible security vulnerability.
Findings require manual interpretation and validation.
